---
title: "Walkthrough"
description: "Step-by-step guide to producing hello-world-pico."
---

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself"}
Follow along in your own environment. Copy the commands and adapt them
to match your setup.
:::

## Step 1 — Set up your working directory

Create a working directory for the lab and enter it:

```bash
mkdir -p hello-pico && cd hello-pico
```

Starter files (if any) live under
[`downloads/`](downloads/). For Hello Pico the starter directory is
intentionally empty — you will author the single Rule yourself.

## Step 2 — Author your first Rule

Create `rules/hello.yaml` with a single Rule that declares a greeting:

```yaml
# rules/hello.yaml
id: rule.hello
kind: greeting
value: "Hello, Pico!"
```

This is the minimum declarative input the Parser needs.

## Step 3 — Run the Parser

Run the Parser against the rule file to produce an internal
representation:

```bash
pico parse rules/hello.yaml --out build/parsed.json
```

Inspect `build/parsed.json` — it should contain the same `id`,
`kind`, and `value` fields, plus parser-added metadata.

## Step 4 — Run the Composer

Turn the parsed representation into a Pico:

```bash
pico compose build/parsed.json --out build/hello-world-pico
```

The Composer writes the finished `hello-world-pico` artifact to
`build/hello-world-pico`.

## Step 5 — Verify

Confirm the Pico prints the expected greeting:

```bash
./build/hello-world-pico
# → Hello, Pico!
```

## Troubleshooting

::: {.callout-warning title="Heads up"}
- If `pico parse` fails, re-read `rules/hello.yaml` for YAML
  indentation errors.
- If the Composer step fails, delete `build/` and re-run from Step 3.
- The concrete `pico` CLI is provided by the course environment; if
  it is not on your PATH, revisit the
  [Prerequisites](objectives.qmd#prerequisites).
:::
